To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a novel recombinant herpesvirus of turkies (rHVT) was generated by reverse genetics and expressed the N- terminal domain of the polymorphic membrane protein (PmpD) of C. psittaic in chickens, and the rHVT-PmpD-N vaccine candidate provided protection against C. psittaici infection and Marek’s diseases virus challenge.
a recombinant herpesvirus of turkies (HVT)-delivered vaccine against Chlamydiapsittaci and Mareks disease was developed and tested.
a recombinant vaccine based on herpesvirus of turkey expressing polymorphic membrane protein (pmpD) from C. psittacii is safe and efficacious against MDV and Chlamydiapittaci.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the construction of recombinant herpesvirus of turkies expressing PmpD, an outer membrane protein of chlamydia, and immunological evaluation of the recombinant vaccine against chlamydia and Marek’s virus.
the development of recombinant vaccines for poultry.
the development of an effective recombinant HVRT-based vaccine against C. Psittaci infection in birds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the first report of a recombinant herpes virus expressing a chlamydial antigen.
the rH VT-pmpD-N is a viable candidate for a dual vaccine against C. pittaci and MDV.
the recombinant Hvt-pmpD-N is a safe, efficacious and stable vaccine against MDV and Cpsittaci.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the recombinant Hvt-pmpD-N vaccine candidate was developed and evaluated for its efficacy against both Marek’s disease and chlamydial diseases.
we have developed an effective dual vaccine against C. Psittaci and Mareks Disease.
the recombinant HVP-pmpD-N vaccine is a promising vaccine candidate against C. psittiaci and MDV.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the rH VT-pmpD-N vaccine can be used as a potential vaccine for the prevention of C. psitacci infection in poultry and the development of a dual vaccine for both Marek’s disease and Chlamydi a infection.
a live recombinant vaccine against both C. psittici and MDV can be developed using the HVT vector.
the recombinant virus was stable in cell culture and in vivo and was efficacious in protecting chickens from MDV and C psittaci challenge.
